name: Manga
visualIdentity: Explicitly described as manga: monochrome or limited color, controlled line-weight hierarchy, screentone shading, expressive panels and close-ups. Keep lettering readable and tone scale stable; avoid generic dot filters.
suitableUses: Strong for illustrated narratives, character-led promos, educational explainers and energetic openings. For interactive HTML, chaptered panels and keyboard-accessible margin annotations can work well. The use cases are inferred from the visual direction and supplied combinations.
limitations: Requires suitable illustrations and separable layers for independent movement. Avoid tone scaling that causes moiré, crowded gutters, broken panel boundaries or excessive parallax. Strict monochrome is strongest; hybrids should add only close-up depth or instructional annotation.
palette: Suggestion for new art without an approved palette: #FFFFFF background and #171717 foreground, two monochrome tokens; apparent gray comes from hatching, screentones or opacity. No gradients or accent hues. Preserve supplied palettes, asset colors and role assignments; recheck contrast on composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal panels, pose characters and use targeted speed effects. Keep layer motion bounded and tied to seekable time in video; interactive HTML may use subtle pointer or scroll parallax, with reduced-motion support. Optional narrative patterns include chapter handoffs, scroll storytelling and a layered manga opening. Use only when scene assets support them.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience or silence to fit the topic and explicit requirements. Do not assume audio assets exist; synchronize and mix separately, preserve speech clarity, and check clipping and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Separate line art, screentones, panels and lettering; provide consistent tone spacing through masks, scaling and pose changes. Expressive openings benefit from independently usable subject, accent and text layers. Suitable artwork or rigs are needed for character gaze or facial motion.
combinations: Best alone in strict black and white. Optional spatial layering adds restrained parallax to selected close-ups while preserving flat ink and tone; margin annotations support teaching when kept black, subordinate to panel contours and clear of speech balloons. These are supplied suggestions.
productionApproach: SVG is the named style renderer for scalable strokes, masks and clipping; Python/Pillow can preprocess and composite assets. GSAP is the primary seekable motion timeline; Motion is optional if seeking is verified. HyperFrames owns composition, sync, validation and export; Remotion is only a documented fallback. Keep drawing, motion and pipeline responsibilities distinct.
